bottom_line: Split the data. Keep the 10-minute Website site small (static files about 0.3 MB gzipped) and move the bulk data (about 358 MB raw, about 71 MB gzipped per full deploy) to a daily or monthly deploy of a second repository's own GitHub Pages site. One Pages site is replaced whole on every deploy, so bulk data kept in the 10-minute site would be re-uploaded up to 144 times a day. The 10-minute cadence is not delivered today: 17 scheduled runs in 52 hours, median gap 151 minutes. hail-store.yml is not on main (GitHub returns 404 for it), so the daily store job is not scheduled.
recommendation: 1) Layout. Main repo (10-minute Pages site): HTML, CSS, JS, fonts, basemap, data/map.json and a small per-town hail summary written by the daily job. The 10-minute build should stop downloading and copying the store. Today only branch builds with --hail-history download it; main does not. Data repo (new, project Pages site at https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/): hail store, address shards and search index, street tiles, footprint shards, climate tiles (25,902 Montana land cells; 4,568 tiles; median 2.0 KB per tile; 8.7 MB raw and 1.2 MB gzip for all tiles), snow and stations (the 45 candidate stations' .dly files, 33.7 MB, not all 481 at 392 MB). Browsers fetch those files cross-origin; access-control-allow-origin: * was verified on this repo's Pages site, and gzip on JSON was verified on data/map.json. 2) Cadence. Daily job (hail store, joins, climate day, stations day): about 12 to 15 minutes, of which the hail build is 612 s (measured in CI on 2026-10-18), joins about 100 s (measured locally), pack and publish under 10 s. Monthly job (addresses: 65.8 MB zip, build 37 s, verify 9 to 39 s, all measured locally; climate: one scaled month, 41 to 57 MB, sources publish 4 to 68 days after month end) and an annual or on-change streets and footprints pass in separate jobs, so each stays under the 60-minute timeout set in hail-store.yml. 3) Browser budget at zoom 15 over Billings (details in measurements.browser_budget): dots, one street tile and footprint shards together are about 607 KB gzipped for a 390x844 phone view. Footprints at zoom 15 are the largest item (193 KB); moving footprints to zoom 16 and up cuts the phone view to about 393 KB (about 8 s on the Slow 3G preset). Footprints at zoom 13 would be about 797 KB and must not load there. 4) Egress. Fetching the 26.4 MB combined store on every 10-minute run would be about 3.8 GB a day (144 runs). The observed rate of 7.8 scheduled starts a day gives about 0.2 GB a day. Pages browser transfer is about 0.6 MB per phone visit at zoom 15, so the 100 GB a month soft limit is about 165,000 such visits. 5) The owner must set the 3G target: the repo does not define one. The figures here use the DevTools Slow 3G preset, about 50 KB/s with a 400 ms round-trip target.

open_questions: The owner must set the 3G target. This record uses the DevTools Slow 3G preset (about 50 KB/s, 400 ms RTT), which is not written in the repo.

Climate and stations: the climate worker's record gives 25,902 land cells, which replaces the 30,000 figure in the brief. The five-year tile size is measured with one record per cell written five times (a stand-in); water-year totals add about 30 bytes per cell (estimate). The aggregate cache per month (1.2 MB) is an estimate.
The station worker's final record was not in the folder when this was written. Station sizes here are full-history file sizes, not the five-year extract.
Footprint geodatabase read (GDAL or FileGDB) and the footprint shard writes were not timed; the footprint quadtree was timed without writing files.
Streets: simplification and tile writes for the whole state were not timed; the MSL statewide run in the streets record took 629 s in that worker's pipeline.
Pages deploy time for a 358 MB site was not measured; the upload action's README advises keeping the tar under 1 GB because larger deploys are more likely to exceed the 10-minute deployment timeout.
The Pages settings were not read through the API (the proxy blocks that path), so the publishing source is taken from the working site and the workflow's own check.

Whether a second repository can serve its Pages site to the main site is not tested beyond the header check on this repo's site. The ACAO header is measured; the data site's own headers should be checked on first deploy.
The GitHub Pages usage text about online businesses (quoted in terms) needs a reading against this site's purpose by the owner or counsel.
The 10-minute cron on main does not deliver 10-minute runs. The median gap is 151 minutes. Whether an external trigger (repository dispatch from another scheduler) would fix this was not tested.

The B3 address folder was being rebuilt during measurement; figures are from 03:04 to 03:14 UTC and agree within 0.2 percent. The precheck shows 4,212 shards and 43.5 MB; the build shows 4,211 and 43.1 MB.
The TIGER edition is named two ways (2025 in streets.json, 2026 in streets-msl-vs-tiger.json). The zip totals differ by 809 bytes; the size is the same either way.

Tile grids differ: the B1 hail grid has tile edges at whole tenths of a degree, while the streets record uses edges at 0.05-degree offsets. One grid should be chosen before sharding; the Billings viewport crosses two B1 tiles but one streets tile.
The Microsoft footprint set (773,199, ODbL share-alike) is smaller by count but uses a different licence; its size is a record estimate, not a file measurement.

The station worker's 80 percent coverage rule was tested only at two points; the coverage of all 481 stations was not computed, so the station subset size for the whole state is not measured (45 candidates for two points is 33.7 MB).
download_note: All downloads were kept in one folder under the scratch folder, deleted after this record was written. Derived copies (B2 and B3 store snapshots, extraction tests) were made from other folders and deleted too.
